stories.title: Documentarian Helps 103-yo D-Day Survivor Recover His Lost War Medals–Just in Time for Veterans Day
stories.label: people
stories.summary: A 103-year-old D-Day veteran just got his long-lost war medals back, right in time for Veterans Day. An amateur WWII historian stumbled across the man's military record and tracked down the family to ask if he still had them. He didn't, so the historian helped track the missing medals down and got them returned. It's a touching reminder that someone's service is never forgotten, even a lifetime later. The whole family is overjoyed to have this piece of his history back where it belongs.
stories.why_good: A real event that reunited an elderly veteran with meaningful lost history, told with warmth and no controversy.

stories.title: China Switches on World's Biggest Liquid-Air Renewable Energy Storage System
stories.label: technology
stories.summary: China just turned on the world's largest liquid-air energy storage facility, a clever system that banks extra renewable power by chilling air into liquid and then releasing it to generate electricity when it's needed. It's a cheap, simple way to store wind and solar energy so it's available even when the sun isn't shining or the wind isn't blowing. This kind of storage is a big missing piece for a cleaner power grid, and now there's real proof it can work at massive scale. It's a solid step toward a future with fewer fossil fuels and more reliable green energy.
stories.why_good: A real, working piece of infrastructure now exists that helps solve one of clean energy's biggest challenges: storage. It benefits the planet and happened, not just a plan.
